interpretation.rate: Sinus tachycardia, rate variable at ~101 bpm (range 90–118). HR elevated and variable 90–118 bpm (avg 101). Compared to raga (avg 91 bpm, later session), guitar produced higher peak rate, greater variability, and no sustained deceleration.
interpretation.rhythm: Regular sinus rhythm with physiologic rate variation. No ectopic beats.
interpretation.p_waves: Upright in I, II, aVF. Inverted in aVR. Normal sinus P waves.
interpretation.qrs_complex: Narrow (86ms). Good R-wave progression V1→V5. No BBB.
interpretation.st_segments: Isoelectric in all leads. No ST elevation or depression.
interpretation.t_waves: Upright in I, II, III, aVF, V3–V6. Inverted in aVR. Normal.
notable_findings: Elevated and variable heart rate 107→118→94→90→105 bpm during guitar stimulus
Peak rate 118 bpm — sympathetic activation/arousal response
Significant baseline artifact in limb leads at recording start (physical guitar playing)
Rate variability higher than raga recording — less autonomic regularity
QT appropriately shortened (308ms) compared to raga (355ms) due to higher rate
Clinically: guitar induced sympathetic activation vs raga's parasympathetic engagement
Recorded BEFORE raga (06:02 PM vs 06:08 PM)
interpretation.overall_assessment: Sinus tachycardia with variable rate during guitar music stimulus. HR reached 118 bpm and remained elevated and variable (~101 bpm avg) throughout, consistent with a sympathetic/arousal autonomic response. Contrast with subsequent raga recording which produced progressive HR deceleration to 80 bpm — demonstrating distinct autonomic signatures between the two musical stimuli.
